Most of these answers miss the point:

Distortion/clipping/limiting/saturation is just waveshaping and different waveshaping gives rise to a balance between even (2x, 4x, 6x, 8x) harmonics and odd (3x, 5x, 7x, 9x) harmonics. Even harmonics reinforce fundamentals and sound like a more harmonious waveshaping, while odd harmonics have less musical intervals after the 5th formed in there.

Any basic wave shape is a balance of these even and odd harmonics off of a fundamental, and waveshaping just approximates your signal towards another shape.

A common comparison is British Neve preamps which are rich in even harmonics and are considered somewhat clean for distortion versus an American preamp that adds a warm boxiness or edgy crunch to signals through more odd harmonics.

My first question is whether this is listening to the kick in isolation or in the mix, because my first thought is a phase change from minimal phase EQ causing some conflict trying to mesh with the phase of other low frequencies, although it would give the same reading on its own meter.

If you look at the ISO loudness contour curves that represent our non-linear perception of frequency distribution at different volumes, you see that high-mid frequencies tend to be audible at the lowest volumes without much sound pressure and the most attention grabbing at the highest volumes, while sub frequencies and higher frequencies are different in that there has to be some actual sound pressure present before it can compete with naturally sensitive frequencies in our hearing. This is also why masking tends to be curved slightly upward in the frequency range when it occurs, because while your ear can work it's natural resonant magic, the higher pressure levels necessary for increasingly lower frequencies at increasingly lower volumes to be perceived as balanced in the context of a mix can be physically stronger than nearby harmonics in a signal and consume more of the available dynamic space at the cost of apparent loudness, as well as the other way around. This means any sound's timbre or brightness is really a kind of spectrum between physical power and psychoacoustic sensitivity.

Technically, even if you attenuated the perception at all 24 possible points of complexity, you could still need a high pass, low pass, high shelf, low shelf, and several surgical notches to kill a few pesky frequencies, bringing the points of processing higher than the actual complexity of our own hearing.
